title: Controllable interaction between photons and distant spins via vacuum Rabi oscillations
authors: Xiao Xue, Jurgen Dijkema, Tobias Bonsen, Patrick Harvey-Collard, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, Sander L. de Snoo, Guoji Zheng, Amir Sammak, Giordano Scappucci, Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
abstract: Vacuum Rabi oscillations between a single photon and a single spin demonstrate the capability of harnessing light-matter interaction at the level of a single quantum of energy. Since the observation of strong spin-photon coupling in gate-defined quantum dots, probing this interaction in the time-domain has been a major objective. Here, we carefully engineer a device composed of two spatially separated double quantum dots hosting single electron spin qubits and a superconducting cavity to accommodate microwave photons. We observe multiple vacuum Rabi oscillations between each spin qubit and the cavity. By concatenating vacuum Rabi oscillations involving the two spins, an energy excitation in one qubit can be emitted as a photon and then transferred to the other qubit. When a single photon is emitted, the cavity is prepared in a Fock state, leading to an accelerated vacuum Rabi frequency. These results serve as building blocks not only in exploring light-matter interactions, but also in interfacing semiconductor spin qubits to photonic links.
summary: The paper reports on the realization of controlled light-matter interaction between two distant electron spin qubits mediated by a microwave cavity. By observing vacuum Rabi oscillations and implementing state transfer protocols, the authors demonstrate that single excitations can be coherently shuttled from one qubit to another via a photon. This work establishes fundamental building blocks for integrating solid-state quantum memories with photonic communication channels.
main_problem: The goal is to demonstrate controllable interaction between photons and distant electron spins using vacuum Rabi oscillations, thereby creating a functional interface between semiconductor spin qubits and photonic quantum links.
main_result: The authors successfully observed multiple vacuum Rabi oscillations and demonstrated the coherent transfer of single excitations from one spin qubit, through the cavity photon, to a second, spatially separated spin qubit.
method: The experiment involves pulsing the system through resonant and dispersive regimes using voltage controls on double quantum dots coupled to a superconducting microwave cavity resonator.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an engineered semiconductor-superconductor hybrid device containing two double quantum dots hosting single electron spin qubits ($	ext{Q1}$ and $	ext{Q2}$) coupled to a microwave cavity. The dynamics are governed by the interplay between spin, photon, and charge degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Vacuum Rabi oscillation frequency ($\Omega_{	ext{Rabi}}$), spin population probabilities ($P_\uparrow$), and the acceleration factor of the Rabi frequency when multiple excitations are present.
important_parameters: Interdot detuning ($\epsilon$), external magnetic field strength/orientation, cavity loss rates ($\gamma$), and coupling strengths ($g_s$).
main_assumptions: The state transfer protocol requires both qubits to start in their ground states; deviations from ideal acceleration are attributed to energy loss and dephasing during the initial photon emission.
figures_summary: Figures show vacuum Rabi oscillation data vs. time/detuning, schematics of spin-photon-spin coupling, and plots illustrating accelerated oscillations corresponding to different initial photon numbers.
paper_structure: The work progresses from demonstrating basic single-qubit VROs, to implementing controlled state transfer between two distant spins via the cavity, and finally analyzing the underlying physics by studying the asymmetry of VROs versus detuning ramps.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it directly addresses quantum networking concepts by realizing controllable entanglement generation (spin-photon-spin) using solid-state qubits coupled to superconducting cavities, a core area of cavity QED and open quantum systems research.

The quantum information encoded in spin qubits can be exchanged into microwave photons in the resonators, which can either be transferred to another qubit in a different module, or transduced to an optical photon in a quantum internet. b. Spintronics.note: The experimental realization of controlled light-matter interaction between two distant electron spin qubits mediated by a microwave cavity directly relates to the 'cavity QED' and 'spin pumping/coherent emission in hybrid spin-photon systems' aspects central to spintronics.
